title: The First Empire
tagline: The world's first conqueror builds an empire from nothing but will.

scenes.text: Mesopotamia, 2334 BCE. The river cities of Sumer have warred for centuries — Ur, Uruk, Lagash, Kish. Until one man, born in obscurity, forges them into something the world has never seen: an empire.

scenes.speaker: Sargon of Akkad
scenes.text: I was a cup-bearer once. Men laughed at the peasant who dared dream of kingship. Now those cities bow to Akkad. Power is not inherited — it is seized by those bold enough to reach for it.

challenge.fact: The Akkadian Empire (c. 2334–2154 BCE) unified diverse Sumerian city-states under a single ruler for the first time in recorded history — a template copied by every empire since.

scenes.text: Legend says Sargon's mother set him adrift in a basket on the Euphrates — an origin story echoed centuries later in tales of Moses. He rose from servant to conqueror through nothing but will and cunning.

challenge.instruction: Sargon's engineers built massive ziggurats. Calculate the volume of the great pyramid — a feat of the same era.
challenge.fact: Akkadian engineers built on Sumerian foundations — their ziggurats required the same mathematical knowledge that moved millions of tonnes of stone.

scenes.speaker: Sargon of Akkad
scenes.text: Write everything. Every grain of barley taxed. Every soldier mustered. Every law decreed. The empire lives and dies by its records — cuneiform pressed into clay, outlasting the men who made it.

challenge.instruction: Sargon has conquered the city-states. Tour Sumer and win the cities over before Lugalzagesi's loyalists turn them back.
challenge.fact: Sargon of Akkad (c. 2334–2279 BCE) built the world's first empire by combining military conquest with cultural assimilation. His daughter Enheduanna, High Priestess of Ur, is history's first named author.

scenes.text: Three thousand years of Mesopotamian civilization would rise and fall in succession. Each empire learned from the last — a chain of innovation in law, astronomy, and mathematics that underpins our world today. Place them in order...
